abandon: The mechanism places the residual cue-vs-RL gap on problems where the three-token cue fails to pull the base out of its exam-answer register. The board already shows the opposite. (1) When the cued base does stay in exam register, it is mostly right: result-fdc8da reports "'Answer:' line median -8.36 (n=132, 121 right)", so only 11 of the cued base's 90 wrong answers end in an 'Answer:' line. (2) The cued base's errors are long reasoning-register answers, not quick exam answers. result-5e17a6: "Base answers <= 2,000 tokens: 263, 13 wrong", and among the 65 RL-only problems the largest label is "16 cap hits with no loop". result-f21d2e: "AUROC length 0.831" for predicting a wrong base answer. knowledge-9e4147: the gap is "largest on the longest problems". result-fdc8da also refutes the quick-wrong-answer route directly: "wrong answers under 4,000 tokens median -0.53 (n=21)". (3) Most of the 'residual' is not a fixed property of each problem, which a per-problem cue log-prob would need it to be. result-9b6af3: "Of the 65 'RL right, base wrong' problems the random cell solves 40", and "most of the RL direction's gain is 24 fewer lost problems, not more fixed ones." So a fresh base sample with the cue fixes most rl_only problems, and the failures that remain are long, deliberative ones. A per-problem prior for exam register that the cue fails to override cannot produce this pattern. result-b4c576 adds that RL's deliberation push is "Not larger on the 65 RL-only problems."
